textContent.text: A conflict on the nearby island of Cuba provided the perfect dramatic material to keep newspaper readers engaged. At the time, Cuba was a Spanish colony, which means that Cuba was governed by Spain. In 1895, Cuban rebels began fighting against Spanish authorities. In response, the Spanish governor of Cuba forced hundreds of thousands of rural Cubans into guarded camps. Conditions in these overcrowded camps were terrible, leading to widespread disease and starvation.

The suffering in Cuba was an ideal topic for yellow journalism in the United States. The American public was eager for news about the conflict, and journalists used this interest to sell newspapers. As a result of this news coverage, many people in the United States sympathized with Cuban rebels against their Spanish rulers.

textContent.text: A conflict on the nearby island of Cuba provided the perfect dramatic material to keep newspaper readers engaged. At the time, Cuba was a Spanish colony, which means that Cuba was governed by Spain. In 1895, Cuban rebels began fighting against Spanish authorities. In response, the Spanish governor of Cuba forced hundreds of thousands of rural Cubans into guarded camps. Conditions in these overcrowded camps were terrible, leading to widespread disease and starvation.

The suffering in Cuba was an ideal topic for yellow journalism in the United States. The American public was eager for news about the conflict, and journalists used this interest to sell newspapers. As a result of this news coverage, many people in the United States sympathized with Cuban rebels against their Spanish rulers.
